name: Pulmonary Sequestration

criteria.description: Presence of nonfunctional lung tissue supplied by an aberrant systemic artery
Lack of normal connection between sequestered lung tissue and bronchial tree
Radiologic evidence of sequestered lung segment on CT or MRI with systemic arterial supply
Recurrent localized pulmonary infections or respiratory distress

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (aberrant arterial supply, absence of bronchial connection, and imaging confirmation) must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiologic and surgical confirmation may be required

pathognomonic.symptomName: Aberrant systemic arterial supply to lung tissue
Nonfunctional lung tissue separated from bronchial tree

common.symptomName: Respiratory distress in infancy or childhood

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers may be elevated during infection
imaging: CT angiography showing aberrant systemic arterial supply
Chest X-ray showing localized opacity or cystic lesion
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; congenital malformation
other: Surgical pathology confirming nonfunctional lung tissue without bronchial connection

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cystic lung lesions with normal pulmonary arterial supply
Connection to bronchial tree usually present
Cystic mass with no systemic arterial supply

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress in neonate or infant
Recurrent severe pulmonary infections unresponsive to antibiotics
references: Stocker JT. Pulmonary Sequestration. In: Stocker JT, Dehner LP, editors. Pediatric Pathology. 3rd ed. Philadelphia: Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2001.
Savic B, Birtel FJ, Tholen W, Funke HD, Knoche R. Lung sequestration: report of seven cases and review of 540 published cases. Thorax. 1979;34(1):96-101.
Corbett HJ, Humphrey GM. Pulmonary sequestration. Paediatr Respir Rev. 2004;5(1):59-68.
